chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who divorces a woman, can he marry her sister? He said: No, until her waiting period (iddah) has expired.

He said, And I asked him about a man who owned two sisters, can he sleep with both of them together? He said: He can sleep with one of them, and when he sleeps with the second one, the first one which he slept with becomes prohibited to him until the second one dies or he separates from her; and it is not for him to sell the second one due to the first in order to return to her, except if he sells for a need, or gives her in charity, or she dies.
He said, And I asked him about a man who had a wife, so she died, can he marry her sister? So he said: From that very moment, if he desires.

key_terms.يَطَأُهُمَا: To sleep with/have relations with them

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for marrying two sisters simultaneously in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between marriage and concubinage regarding the prohibition of 'Gathering between two sisters' (Jam' al-Ukhtayn). It establishes that while a man may hold two sisters in concubinage simultaneously, consummation with the second renders the first temporarily prohibited until she dies or is freed, whereas death of the first wife allows immediate marriage to the second. The ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that the prohibition is based on concurrent possession rather than an absolute ban, distinguishing it from the permanent prohibition of marrying two sisters simultaneously in marriage.
